issues.legal_issue: A tribunal’s finding that a claimed family partition was not genuine and not acted upon could be upheld where it was based on material in the record.
material_facts: The family’s karta claimed that a partition had occurred and sought tax relief and recognition of the partition.
The Income-tax Officer, the appellate authority and the Tribunal rejected the claim; the Tribunal found on the material before it that the partition was not acted upon.
The High Court answered against the taxpayer the referred question whether legal evidence supported the Tribunal’s finding.
issues.conclusion: The High Court was right to uphold the Tribunal’s finding; no question of law arose for the Supreme Court to decide, and the taxpayer’s appeal was dismissed with costs.
issues.legal_principle: A tribunal’s finding on whether a partition was genuine and acted upon, when made on material before it, did not give rise to a question of law warranting interference in this appeal. The taxpayer had sought relief under sections 25A and 25(4) of the Income-tax Act, and the matter reached the High Court by reference under section 66(2), following the procedure in section 66(1). No earlier cases were cited.

predicates.tax_reference_appeal: The case is an appeal arising from a tax-law reference concerning a tribunal’s finding.
predicates.tribunal_made_finding_on_partition_from_: The tribunal considered material in the record and found that the claimed family partition was not acted upon.

issues.definition: If an appeal arising from a tax reference challenges a tribunal’s record-based finding that a claimed partition was not acted upon, the taxpayer’s appeal is dismissed.

issues.legal_issue: A tribunal’s finding that a claimed family partition was genuine could be upheld when additional material before it supported that finding.
material_facts: In a later tax proceeding, the claimed partition was evidenced by a deed different in date from the partition considered in the earlier proceeding.
A civil court had found the deed genuine, fair and binding and found that the joint family had ceased to exist.
The Tribunal had additional material, including sworn statements by the sons and other relevant material, supporting the partition, while making an exception concerning one house.
The High Court found material supporting the Tribunal’s finding, and the Commissioner appealed.
issues.conclusion: The High Court was right that there was material supporting the Tribunal’s finding that the partition was genuine; the Commissioner’s appeal was dismissed with costs.
issues.legal_principle: A tribunal’s finding that a partition was genuine may stand where additional material supports it, including sworn statements and other relevant material; a finding concerning a differently evidenced partition in an earlier proceeding does not eliminate the support available for the finding in the later proceeding. The later application was under section 25A of the Income-tax Act, and the reference proceeded under sections 66(1) and 66(2). No earlier cases were cited.

predicates.tax_reference_appeal: The case is an appeal arising from a tax-law reference concerning a tribunal’s finding.
predicates.tribunal_considered_additional_partition: The tribunal considered additional evidence and relevant material concerning whether the family partition was genuine.
predicates.sons_gave_sworn_statements: The family members’ sons gave statements on oath supporting the claimed partition.
predicates.asserted_partition_differed_from_earlier: The partition asserted in the proceeding was evidenced differently from the partition considered in an earlier proceeding.

issues.definition: If a Commissioner’s appeal arising from a tax reference concerns a partition finding supported by additional material, sworn statements by the sons, and a claim differing from the one considered earlier, the Commissioner’s appeal is dismissed.
